tags.gist: Says the two-axis framework describes the commenter's offline bystander-emergency app almost exactly, but the no-clinician setting is undiscussed and changes several answers.
Wants time pressure and downstream safeguards as first-class dimensions, and protocol fidelity rather than open-endedness as the primary modifier for lay-rescuer guidance.
Says bystander outputs should be action-directing; the real modifiers are premise fidelity, age-appropriate technique and call ordering, warranting a protocol-delivery sub-category.
Lists safeguards to count as mitigants: rule-based selection of high-consequence protocols, refusal that redirects rather than abandons, and frozen on-device operation.
Says that for protocol delivery, escalation belongs to every protocol as a step, judged by its ordering per scenario rather than as a scalar trade-off.
Says mechanical scanning is no release check; wants premise-sensitive test items adjudicated by humans, with sponsor benchmarks published in full instead of being required independent.
Would make the unaided user the primary comparator where the intended use is explicitly for when no professional is available.
Says frozen models on the device neither drift nor report home, so re-benchmarking after changes plus field-report intake should be their duty, unlike hosted models.
Says pinned, hash-checked weights on the device settle third-party change detection by construction; fine-tuning an open-weight model from a fixed base counts as manufacturer control.
Asks the guidance to address explicitly the setting where nothing stands behind the device, rather than a clinician.
Introduces the offline emergency-guidance product and says the no-clinician, no-cloud setting goes undiscussed in the paper yet changes its answers.
Wants time pressure and downstream safeguards treated as one first-class axis, with consequences judged against what care would happen without the device.
Would rank traceability to published protocols first for lay-rescuer guidance, measuring departures from the protocol as the hazard and primary risk modifier.
Agrees disclaimers do not reduce directiveness, but says for bystander emergencies the modifiers are premise fidelity, age-appropriate technique and when the call for help comes.
Asks the guidance to recognize a protocol-delivery sub-category of action-directing function, judged by fidelity to a published protocol.
Asks that deterministic protocol selection, refusal that redirects to the nearest safe action, and offline on-device operation be recognized as risk mitigants.
Says bystander functions make escalation a protocol step, so it should be scored as scenario-specific ordering fidelity rather than a trade-off between error rates.
Wants premise-aware items with human adjudication, age-stratified negatives, and full disclosure of sponsor benchmarks instead of an independence requirement.
Says the honest comparator for the offline setting is an untrained person acting from memory, with the standard of care only second.
Says offline models produce no logs and cannot drift, so re-benchmarking on change should be primary and frozen models distinguished from hosted ones.
Says hash-verified shipped weights leave no third-party change to detect, and asks that fixed-version open-weight models count as manufacturer-controlled.
Asks the eventual guidance to speak explicitly to settings without network or clinician, where a home-triage rule would be ignored or block the product.
